we have identified and characterized genes that are differentially expressed during abalone development and have used this information to construct a developmental cDNA microarray.
we have identified a number of genes that appear to be important in the growth and development of the tropical abalone, Haliois asinina.

understanding the genetic basis of growth, development and shell formation in the tropical abalone, Haliois asinina.
understanding how genes are controlled during abalone development, growth and reproduction.
the identification of genes that control growth, development and shell formation in abalone.

this study has provided an important resource for future investigations of the development, physiology and ecology of the tropical abalone, and indeed all haliotids.

the ESTs obtained here provide a useful resource for the study of the development, growth, and reproduction of the tropical abalone H. asinima, and will provide a basis for future microarray analysis of this and other abalone species.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have generated a cDNA library from a Haliotis developmental stage and sequenced 232 EST clones.
the ESTs obtained in this study provide a valuable resource for future studies in abalone biology.
this study has provided a foundation for future detailed analyses of abalones growth, development, reproduction, and shell formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EST sequencing is a powerful tool for the identification of genes involved in the development, growth, and reproduction of abalone and other marine mollusks.
EST analysis is a valuable and cost-effective tool for the identification of genes that may have a role in growth, development and shell formation in H. as inina and related abalone.
ESTs can be a valuable tool for the identification of genes expressed in specific tissues or at particular times during development.
